questions.q: A ground receiver receives a signal at $5 \mathrm{MHz}$, transmitted by a ground transmitter at a height of $320 \mathrm{~m}$, which is $110 \mathrm{~km}$ away from it. Then it can communicate through (radius of earth $R=6400 \mathrm{~km}$ )
options: space waves
ground waves
sky waves
both sky and ground waves
questions.solution:
Maximum distance covered by space wave communication
$=\sqrt{2 R h}=\sqrt{2\left(6400 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m}\right)(320 \mathrm{~m})}=64 \mathrm{~km}$
Since the distance between transmitter and receiver is $110 \mathrm{~km}$, therefore the given frequency signal cannot communicate through either by ground waves or space waves.
For sky wave, the value of critical frequency is
$\begin{aligned} v_c & =9\left(N_{\max }\right)^{1 / 2}=9\left(10^{12}\right)^{1 / 2} \\ & =9 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}=9 \mathrm{MHz}\end{aligned}$
where, $N_{\max }=$ Maximum electron density of ionosphere.
As the signal frequency $5 \mathrm{MHz} < 9 \mathrm{MHz}$, so the communication is through sky waves.

questions.q:
Assertion : Television signals are received through sky-wave propagation.
Reason : The ionosphere reflects electromagnetic waves of frequencies greater than a certain critical frequency.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
In sky wave propagation, the radio waves having frequency range $2 \mathrm{MHz}$ to $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ are reflected back by the ionosphere. Radio waves having frequency nearly greater than $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ penetrates the ionosphere and is not reflected back by the ionosphere. The TV signal having frequency greater than $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ therefore cannot be propagated through sky wave propagation.
In case of sky wave propagation, critical frequency is defined as the highest frequency that is returned to the earth by the considered layer of the ionosphere after having sent straight to it. Above this frequency, a wave will penetrate the ionosphere and is not reflected by it.

questions.solution:
If the height of the antenna is $h$, then the maximum distance upto which the TV transmission for a TV tower can be received is proportional to $h^{1 / 2}$.
Suppose that the height of the TV antena be $h$ and the radius of the earth be $R and R \gt \gt h$. Let $A$ be a receiving station. In the limit $h\lt \lt R$, we can assume that $B A$ is a tangent to the surface of the earth. Then $\angle B A O=90^{{}^{\circ}} and $so B O²=A B²+A O² \Rightarrow(R+h)^2=A B²+R² \Rightarrow \quad A B²=R²+h²+2 R h-R²=2 R h+h² as$h\lt \lt R$ we neglect $h^2$ and so $\begin{aligned}$& A B²=2 R h \Rightarrow A B=$\sqrt{2 R h}$\\ \therefore \quad & A B \propto h^{1 / 2} . \end{aligned}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In short wave communication, waves of which of the following frequencies will be reflected back by the ionospheric layer having electron density $10^{11}$ per $\mathrm{m}^3$ ?
options: $2 \mathrm{MHz}$
$10 \mathrm{MHz}$
$12 \mathrm{MHz}$
$18 \mathrm{MHz}$.
questions.solution:
We know that the artificial frequency of a sky wave for reflection from an ionospheric layer of the atmosphere is given by, $v_c=9 N^{1 / 2}$ where $n$ is the number density of electrons $/ \mathrm{m}^3$. It is given that $N=10^{11} / \mathrm{m}^3$
\therefore \quad v_c=9 $\times\left($10^{11}\right)^{1 / 2}=2.8 $\times$10^6 $\mathrm{~Hz}=$2.8 $\mathrm{MHz} \text{. }$Hence the wave of frequency $2 \mathrm{MHz}$ will be reflected back.
questions.question: In short wave communication, waves of which of the following frequencies will be reflected back by the ionospheric layer having electron density $10^{11}$ per $\mathrm{m}^3$ ?
questions.explanation:

\therefore \quad v_c=9 \times$\left(10^{11}\right)^{1 / 2}$=2.8 \times 10^6 $\mathrm{~Hz}=$2.8 $\mathrm{MHz}\text{. } $
Hence the wave of frequency $2 \mathrm{MHz}$ will be reflected back.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Assertion : Microwave communication is preferred over optical communication.
Reason : Microwaves provide large number of channels and bandwidth compared to optical signals.
options: if both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
if both assertion and reason are true and the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
if assertion is true but reason is false
if both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution:
The quality of a communication system is determined by its information carrying capacity. The information carrying capacity is directly proportional to its bandwidth. The wider the bandwidth, the greater its information carrying capacity.
As the light frequencies used in optical fibre systems is much larger than the highest frequency microwave transmissions, so the bandwidth in case of optical communication systems is much larger than that in microwave communications. The bandwidth of the optical fibre systems is quite suitable for the present day communication needs and also for the future. That's why optical communication is preferred over microwave communication.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the modulation index of an amplitude modulated wave is changed from 0 to 1 , then the transmitted power will be
options: unchanged
doubled
increased by $50 \%$
zero
questions.solution:
The transmitted power in AM wave is
$P_t=\left(1+\frac{\mu^2}{2}\right) P_c$
where $\mu$ is the modulation index and $P_c$ is the power in carrier wave.
When $\mu=0, P_t=P_c$
and when $\mu=1, P_t=\left(1+\frac{1}{2}\right) P_c=\frac{3}{2} P_c$
$\therefore$ The percentage increase in transmitted power
$=\frac{\frac{3}{2} P_c-P_c}{P_c} \times 100 \%=\frac{1}{2} \times 100 \%=50 \%$
